quote: The *he* + participle form is for what is still open: a view you still hold (*siempre he pensado*, *nunca he entendido*) or a stretch of time you are still in (*este año*, *esta semana*).
problem: This is the core Latin American use of the perfect, yet it first appears at u52 (C1), 44 units after g:perfecto-experience. Meanwhile that A1 script says He is for ever, never and not yet, which excludes Siempre he vivido aquí and Últimamente he estado cansado. A learner has no way to talk about a situation that continues up to now for most of the course, and writes siempre viví aquí or hace que. Move the node to A2, near u23 (g:hace-que-desde) or u26 (g:acabar-de-ya-todavia).
authority: RAE, Nueva gramática, the perfect in American Spanish; PCIC treats the perfect at A1 and A2

quote: Teachers call *mí*, *ti*, *conmigo* and *contigo* prepositional (or tonic) pronouns.
problem: The rule says the forms change after little words, with no exceptions. Entre and según keep yo and tú: entre tú y yo, según tú. English speakers say between you and me, and a transfer of the rule gives *entre ti y mí. No node covers it.
authority: RAE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, entre, según
replacement: Teachers call *mí*, *ti*, *conmigo* and *contigo* prepositional (or tonic) pronouns. Two words break the pattern and keep *yo* and *tú*: *entre tú y yo*, *según tú*.

problem: la parte means part, share or side. "bulletin, report" is el parte, a different masculine noun, yet the entry shows the article la. It is a top-200 noun; every tap on parte in a text says "bulletin, report" and the card teaches it.
authority: DLE, parte (f.) and parte (m.); Collins Spanish-English

problem: The gloss is the false friend itself. desgracia means misfortune or tragedy; English disgrace is deshonra or vergüenza. por desgracia means unfortunately.
The commonest use of solo is the adverb only, used constantly from A1 (Solo hay mango). The gloss gives alone and lonely only, so a tap in a chapter gives the wrong meaning.
authority: RAE, Ortografía 2010 on solo; DLE, solo

problem: solamente never means alone.
In practice this word appears as ni siquiera, not even. "at least" covers only a minor concessive use.

quote: shadow is blocked by the shade of an object)
problem: Corrupted Wiktionary fragment, shown on a taught card: "shadow is blocked by the shade of an object)".
Corrupted Wiktionary markup in a learner gloss: "to benefit ] or +de]".

A taught A1 card (session 105) says el repente means "attack, upsurge". Nobody needs this noun; the learner needs the fixed phrase de repente, suddenly. The tagger reads repente alone and the card teaches a sense that never occurs.
replacement: remove as a lexeme card; teach c:de-repente, suddenly

problem: nuevamente means again. "newly" is wrong and will distort every sentence it appears in.

The base entry for sentido gives only the rare adjective "deeply felt, heartfelt" (mi más sentido pésame). The noun, sense or meaning (no tiene sentido, sentido común, sentido del humor) is a top-500 word and has no entry. Tapping sentido in "no tiene sentido" returns "deeply felt".
The noun el hecho, fact (de hecho, el hecho de que), is a top-300 word and has no entry; the only gloss is the participle sense "done, completed".
The frequency rank comes from llevar a cabo and al cabo de, but the gloss is "cape (geography)", and llevar a cabo occurs nowhere in the bank or chapters.
replacement: end (llevar a cabo = to carry out; al cabo de = after)

problem: As an adjective temporal means temporary, by far the commonest use in news and work Spanish (trabajo temporal). The entry is only the noun storm.
First meaning is alliance. "wedding band" alone misleads in any political text.
First meanings are letter of the alphabet and handwriting; lyrics is a secondary sense. Taught from a song context, then wrong elsewhere.
Primary sense is column (architecture, newspaper). Spine is a derived sense from columna vertebral.
The common use is acostumbrado a, used to. "customary" misleads in Ya estoy acostumbrado (ch184).
The story turns on pruebas as evidence (ch135: el comité quiere pruebas), yet the gloss is only test.
antes de is before. "earlier" alone gives a wrong reading of antes de su viaje.
Only "tall": temporada alta, alta voz and precios altos all need high.
"plain" is a poor first gloss; the commonest meaning is simple or easy.
"track, platform" is a railway sense. In the story la vía 40 is a road, and in news vías means roads or routes.
Primary sense is function; performance is one sense.
plazo means deadline or term, not "period, phase". a largo plazo and en plazo both misread.
tomar medidas (to take steps) and a medida que depend on the sense missing here.
Political party is missing, a core news sense.
en efectivo (cash) appears in ch145 and everywhere else; the noun sense is missing.
"background" misreads al fondo, en el fondo, a fondo and el fondo del salón (ch155).
quieto means still, not moving, not calm. ch165 Hasta Simón se quedó quieto.
enamorado is simply in love.
Stupendous is rarer and more formal than the Spanish word.
camping is the activity; campamento is a camp.
In Colombia paradero is first of all a bus stop; the story is set in Bogota.
With pararse taught as to stand up, parado in Colombia means standing. Stopped, halted is the wrong first gloss here.
Wrong article: musical notes are masculine (el fa). Also junk as a C1 card; it entered from the frequency list.
"C (musical note)" as a taught C1 card is a frequency-list artefact from the English word do in subtitles.
Wrong article and wrong gender field. gestión is feminine, and the learner sees el gestión on tap and in Look up.
Listed as a word with "hindering". The word is only ever met as no obstante, however.
The everyday sense reader should come first.
Its frequency comes from en torno a, about or around. "lathe" is useless to a learner.

quote: Vale se puso la mano en la boca
problem: Calque of "put her hand to her mouth". The idiomatic gesture is llevarse la mano a la boca.
authority: Usage; CORPES XXI collocation llevarse la mano a
replacement: Vale se llevó la mano a la boca

quote: Él fue muy consciente de sus manos en la espalda.
problem: Reads as translated from "He was very aware of her hands on his back". Spanish narrative would say what he felt; the preterite of ser with consciente is stiff and sus is ambiguous. consciente is present because it is the day's target word.
replacement: Tomás sintió las manos de ella en la espalda, y no pensó en otra cosa.

quote: Y no le voy a hacer un truco, como Duarte.
problem: hacer un truco means perform a trick. The sense "pull a trick on you" would be jugarle una mala pasada, or in Colombia hacerle conejo.
authority: Usage; Diccionario de colombianismos, hacer conejo
replacement: Y no le voy a jugar una mala pasada, como Duarte.

quote: no concede vacaciones en temporada alta
problem: A diver speaking about his boss would not say conceder; the verb is there because it is the target lexeme. Register slip caused by lexeme stuffing.
replacement: no da vacaciones en temporada alta
